name: DS1822 1-Wire econo digital thermometer
description: Maxim/Analog Devices econo 1-Wire digital thermometer, -55 to +125 °C (±2 °C from -10 to +85 °C, ±3 °C over the full range), 9-12 bit resolution (0.0625 °C at the default 12 bits, 750 ms conversion), unique 64-bit ROM code with family code 22h, software compatible with the DS18B20. Runs on 3.0-5.5 V. Sold as: DS1822+ in a 3-pin TO-92 through-hole package (datasheet bottom view; with the flat face towards you and legs down: GND, DQ, VDD), needing an external 4.7 kΩ pull-up from DQ to VDD.
eli5: A cheap little thermometer chip that sends the temperature as a number down a single wire; several can share the same wire.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (TO-92 pin 1, left with the flat face towards you)

pins.name: DQ
pins.description: 1-Wire data in/out, open-drain (TO-92 pin 2, middle); needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to VDD

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 3.0-5.5 V (TO-92 pin 3, right). Use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so the pull-up keeps DQ at 3.3 V logic

buildNotes: Pin order with the flat face towards you, legs down: left = GND, middle = DQ, right = VDD (the datasheet drawing is a bottom view). Wired backwards it gets hot fast: unplug it at once.
Fit a 4.7 kΩ pull-up from DQ to VDD and power VDD from 3.3 V when DQ goes to an ESP32 or Pico.

Send Convert T (44h), then wait at least 750 ms (12-bit) before Read Scratchpad (BEh); MicroPython's ds18x20 module does the commands and the CRC check (it recognises family 22h), your code does the wait.
Temperature = signed 16-bit register x 0.0625 °C (same format as the DS18B20). A reading of exactly 85 °C is the power-on value: the conversion did not finish or the sensor lost power.
Accuracy is only ±2 °C (-10 to +85 °C); use a DS18B20 if you need ±0.5 °C.
Use VDD (external power), not parasite power: parasite mode needs VDD grounded and a strong pull-up during every conversion.

example.code:
import machine, onewire, ds18x20, time

ds = ds18x20.DS18X20(onewire.OneWire(machine.Pin({DQ})))
roms = ds.scan()
print('found', len(roms))
while True:
    ds.convert_temp()
    time.sleep_ms(750)  # 12-bit conversion: up to 750 ms
    print('T=%.2fC' % ds.read_temp(roms[0]))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the temperature set on the slider

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (1 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
